text: Good API design makes software easier to use and maintain. When building REST APIs, you should create clear and consistent endpoints that represent resources, such as /users or /orders. Always return the correct HTTP status codes, like 200 for success or 404 when something is not found, so developers understand what happened. Good documentation is also essential, because it helps others learn how to use your API quickly. Finally, use versioning, for example /v1/users, so you can improve your API without breaking existing applications. Following these simple practices leads to APIs that are reliable, friendly, and built to last.
